---
title: "Step 1 — Install R, RStudio and Quarto"
subtitle: "Step 1 of 5"
---

**Time:** 30 minutes, plus download time.
**Before you start:** the laptop you will bring to IISc, and administrator
rights on it.
**When you finish:** R, RStudio and Quarto are installed and working together.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Check your administrator rights now
On an institutional laptop you may not have them. Find out this week, not on
Sunday night. If you cannot install software yourself, ask your IT department
now and send them this page.
:::

## Step 1 of 7 — Install R

1. Go to [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org).
2. Click the link for your operating system.
3. **Windows:** click **base**, then the download link, then run the `.exe` and
   accept every default.
4. **macOS:** click the `.pkg` for your chip. Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4)
   needs the **arm64** build. Older Intel Macs need the plain one. To check,
   click the Apple menu, then **About This Mac**, and read the **Chip** line.
5. **Linux:** follow the CRAN instructions for your distribution. Install from
   the CRAN apt repository, not your distribution's own `r-base`, which is
   usually several versions behind.

**You should see:** an installer that finishes without an error box.

**If it does not work:** install into the default location. A folder path
containing spaces or non-English characters makes package installs fail later,
in ways that are hard to diagnose.

## Step 2 of 7 — Check that R opens

1. Open R on its own. On Windows, choose **R x64** from the Start menu. On
   macOS, open `R.app`.
2. Read the first line in the console window.

**You should see:** a version number of **4.1.0 or higher**. Any current R is
far higher than that.

**If it does not work:** repeat Step 1. Do not go on to RStudio until R itself
opens.

## Step 3 of 7 — Install RStudio

1. Go to
   [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
2. Download the installer the page offers you.
3. Run it and accept the defaults.

**You should see:** RStudio open with 4 panes, and the console at the left
showing the same R version you read in Step 2.

**If it does not work:** if the console says R is missing, close RStudio,
confirm that R itself opens, then install RStudio again.

::: {.callout-note}
## R and RStudio are not the same program
RStudio is a window onto R. Updating RStudio does not update R. Updating R does
not update RStudio. When you update, you have 2 things to update, separately.
:::

## Step 4 of 7 — Install Quarto

1. Go to [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).
2. Download the installer for your system and run it.

**You should see:** an installer that finishes without an error box.

## Step 5 of 7 — Restart your computer

Restart the whole computer, not only RStudio.

**You should see:** your normal desktop after the restart.

**If it does not work:** do not skip this step. Quarto adds itself to your
system PATH. On Windows, programs that were already running cannot see that
change until they restart.

## Step 6 of 7 — Point RStudio at the right R

Do this only if you have used R on this laptop before. More than one R can be
installed at once.

1. Open RStudio.
2. Click **Tools → Global Options → General**.
3. Read the **R version** line at the top.

**You should see:** the R you installed in Step 1.

**If it does not work:** click **Change**, choose the right R, then restart
RStudio.

## Step 7 of 7 — Confirm the native pipe works

1. Click once inside the **Console** pane, at the bottom left.
2. Type `c(1, 2, 3) |> sum()` and press **Enter**.

**You should see:** `[1] 6`.

**If it does not work:** an error here means your R is older than 4.1.0. Go back
to Step 1.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
You are installing 3 separate programs, and the order matters. R is the engine.
RStudio is the editor you sit in front of. Quarto turns your analysis into a
document.

RStudio looks for an existing R when it starts. Installed the other way round,
it reports that R is missing even when it is not.

We use the native pipe `|>` in every session, so Step 7 is a real test and not a
formality.
:::

## Done?
